current_status.to: Replaced. All four facility types covered by Resolution 2025-25 were superseded by their own permanent regulation resolutions, each with an explicit rescission clause tied back to Resolution 2025-25: Resolution 2026-4 (Battery Energy Storage Systems, effective 2026-02-17), Resolution 2026-5 (Data Center Facilities, effective 2026-02-17), Resolution 2026-6 (Solar Energy / Community Solar Garden, effective 2026-02-17), and Resolution 2026-11 (Wind Energy Facilities, adopted 2026-04-07, shortly before the moratorium's own ~2026-04-19 lapse date). None of the four components lapsed unaddressed.
current_status.reason: Logan County's own recorded resolutions (2026-4, 2026-5, 2026-6, 2026-11), fetched directly from logancountyco.gov, each contain rescission language naming the specific facility type from Resolution 2025-25, resolving the prior uncertainty about the non-data-center components.

affected_projects.from: County discussion referenced a possible data center request near the 2 GW scale in northeastern Colorado [VERIFY: 2 GW figure is from county meeting discussion as captured in secondary reporting; no formal application record identified].
affected_projects.to: County Commissioners' October 14, 2025 work-session minutes record a briefing by developer Blake Marcus (Granite Renewables) and consultant Ben Gager (SWCA Environmental Consultants) describing a proposed project east and west of County Road 9 (approximately 21 miles northwest of Sterling) at close to 2 GW nameplate capacity, including 1 GW of on-site natural gas generation, 630 MW of solar as ancillary power, and 1,800 MWh of battery storage. Commissioner Yahn noted the moratorium had already been planned before this specific proposal surfaced. As of a January 2026 hearing, commissioners stated no formal permit application had yet been received.
affected_projects.reason: Logan County Commissioners' Work Session minutes for 2025-10-14 (logancountyco.gov) contain a verbatim quote establishing the 2 GW figure and project description in a primary meeting record, not secondary reporting alone.

evidence.title: Resolution 2026-4 (Battery Energy Storage Systems)
evidence.supports: Rescinds the Battery Energy Storage System component of the Resolution 2025-25 moratorium and adopts permanent BESS regulations
evidence.quote: The temporary moratorium established by Resolution 2025-25 on the issuance of permits related to the operation of Battery Energy Storage System facilities is hereby rescinded.

evidence.title: Resolution 2026-5 (Data Center Facilities)
evidence.supports: Rescinds the Data Center Facility component of the Resolution 2025-25 moratorium and adopts permanent Data Center Facility regulations
evidence.quote: ...permits related to the operation of Data Center facilities is hereby rescinded.

evidence.title: Resolution 2026-6 (Solar Energy / Community Solar Garden regulations)
evidence.supports: Rescinds the Solar Energy component of the Resolution 2025-25 moratorium
evidence.quote: ...permits related to the operation of Solar Energy (Community Solar Garden) facilities is hereby rescinded.

evidence.title: Resolution 2026-11 (Wind Energy Facilities regulations)
evidence.supports: Rescinds the Wind Energy component of the Resolution 2025-25 moratorium, adopted shortly before the moratorium's own term would have lapsed
evidence.quote: ...permits related to the operation of Wind Energy Facilities is hereby rescinded.

evidence.title: Board of County Commissioners Work Session Minutes, October 14, 2025
evidence.supports: Primary-source origin of the 2 GW project-scale figure that prompted Resolution 2025-25
evidence.quote: It will be close to two gigawatts of nameplate. It will include a significant request of power from the grid, and it will include one gigawatt of natural gas generation on site and 630 megawatts of solar as ancillary power. Then there will be 1,800 megawatt hours of battery energy storage.

decisions.notes: The Planning Commission hearing on amended wind regulations was not held until March 17, 2026, per Resolution 2026-11's own recitals, which is why the wind component was the last to be replaced (April 7, 2026, 12 days before the moratorium's own ~180-day lapse date). Sequencing corroborated by Journal-Advocate (Sterling, CO) coverage of the Feb 18, 2026 and Apr 7, 2026 commissioner actions.
